designDecisions: Vocabulary is kebab-case, matching every other enum in the repo. The brief's SCREAMING_SNAKE names map one-for-one.

TEMPLATE_COMPILER_VERSION bumped 2 → 3 because the compiler's output changed (every compile now emits routes[].scope/slotCount, routePolicy and collections). The manifest schema accepts 1..3, so old artifacts still parse; nothing in the repo pins the template compilerVersion to a literal.

structure-only keeps its route in site-map.routes[] with scope+slotCount 0. exclude REMOVES the route from routes[] and lists it in excludedRoutes[] with its reason — that is the 'not represented' distinction, and the manifest still lists it under routes[] because the copied exact app really does still serve it.
A rule that matches no route is a hard input error, and so is a policy that leaves no slotized route: a policy that silently does nothing is exactly the failure this stage exists to prevent.
The policy is a compile-time INPUT file only. No Selector change, no SiteSpec change, no discovery-coverage change, no new release StageRunner, no new DOM attribute.
limitations: A structure-only page renders the ORIGINAL content for EVERYTHING on it, including the header/footer that a global slot edits elsewhere, because it carries no bindings at all. Recorded in the manifest as the limitation code `structure-only-pages-keep-original-content-including-global-slot-values`. For a blog member page this is usually right (the shell is original anyway) but it is a real semantic cost and an operator must know it.

Narrowing the extractor's page set also narrows the global-promotion pool (grouping.ts:434-484 requires a header/footer unit to cover every non-locale page it sees). A policied compile can therefore classify a slot page-scoped that a policy-free compile would have promoted to global. Slot KEYS can differ between the two compiles, so a slot-overrides file written against a policy-free compile is not automatically valid against a policied one.

`exclude` removes the route from the template's represented surface (site map + slots) but the copied exact app still serves it — pruning the app would edit the frozen Exact Reconstruction copy and break parity QA. Recorded as `excluded-routes-still-served-by-the-copied-exact-app`.

site-map routes[].slotCount attributes page-scoped slots to the page's CANONICAL route (the first route serving that page). A family-represented route that shares a slotized page therefore reads slotCount 0 even though it renders slotized content — visible in the canary at /resources/more/virtual-credit-cards-for-businesses-explained.

Collection grouping is by SiteSpec routeScope, falling back to inferredRoutePattern. A family with neither is never a collection member, and two different inferred patterns in one scope collapse detailPattern to null rather than guessing.
semanticKind is a lookup on the URL scope token (blog/docs/news/…): a site that calls its blog /journal gets `other`. It is a naming hint, never a content claim.
fieldHints are the slot roles observed on the representative detail page(s) — not a field schema, and empty when the representative is structure-only.

The LIVE parity proof for structure-only ran on the 2-page smoke fixture. The 20-route stripe canary was proved offline (byte-identical app tree + full binding validation), not through a full qa:recon-template run.
No auto-derivation of a policy exists: an operator writes the rules. Deriving a default policy from the collections model is deliberately left to a later task.

The path-spelling fix covers routePolicy.policyFile only. manifest.source.siteSpecFile and manifest.source.reconstructionManifestFile are still embedded at the caller's spelling, so an absolute-vs-relative invocation of those two arguments still perturbs manifest.json bytes inside the same hashed template dir. Left alone deliberately (out of the brief's scope); filed as a followUp.

portablePath is relative to process.cwd(), so a compile launched from a subdirectory records `../…`. Every pnpm script runs from the repo root, which is the same assumption src/sitespec/load-inputs.ts and src/reconstruction-qa/store.ts already make.

The shared-page count is emitted for `structure-only` routes only. An `exclude`d route sharing a slotized page is not counted separately — it is already declared as still-served by the copied exact app.
The existing canary run directory was NOT recompiled, so its on-disk manifest.limitations still lacks the companion code. The count was proved against the same inputs read-only.
followUps: Auto-suggest a policy: the collections model now carries everything needed to PROPOSE `keep the index + one representative, structure-only the rest`. Emitting a suggested route-policy.json next to the site map would make the feature one-click without making it implicit.

Decide whether a structure-only page should still receive GLOBAL slot values (a header/footer-only binding pass). That is a real product question, not a bug: it would restore chrome editability at the cost of some bindings per page.
Collection-aware content injection: a later stage could write one representative and declare the rest as 'renders the representative's content', instead of leaving them at original content.

If a release ever needs an excluded route to actually 404/disappear, that belongs to the production build stage (src/production, src/release), not to the template compiler — the template must never edit the Exact Reconstruction copy.

Normalize manifest.source.siteSpecFile / source.reconstructionManifestFile through the same portablePath() so the whole template run dir is spelling-independent for the lineage hash — the two on-disk stripe and linear manifests already disagree on this (absolute vs repo-relative).

Consider a repo-wide check (one test, not a refactor) that no artifact under data/ embeds a string starting with the machine's home directory. That would catch the content-run and theme-run pointers the audit flagged, owned elsewhere.

If a future policy legitimately wants a documentation-only rule (a rule kept for a route set that this reconstruction does not contain), it now needs an explicit opt-out — today the guard refuses it, which is the intended strictness.

hardening.finding: 1 — site-map.json bytes depended on how the operator SPELLED the --route-policy argument (src/recon-template/site-map.ts:71 embedded the raw CLI argument), so two logically identical compiles produced different bytes and therefore a spurious release lineage difference.
hardening.fix: The policy file is READ at the caller's spelling and RECORDED repo-relative POSIX — the convention src/sitespec/load-inputs.ts:139 and src/reconstruction-qa/store.ts:165 already use. Normalized once at the resolution boundary (src/recon-template/compile.ts:105-115, `portablePath(policyFile)` reused from ../reconstruction-qa/store.js, not re-written), so ResolvedRoutePolicy.policyFile is portable everywhere it lands: site-map.json routePolicy.policyFile AND manifest.json routePolicy.policyFile.
hardening.proof: scripts/smoke-recon-template.ts §20 compiles the SAME fixture twice with the same policy file spelled absolutely and relatively and compares site-map.json / manifest.json / slots.json / slot-bindings.json byte for byte: identical. Two supporting checks keep it honest — 'the two spellings really are different strings' (the test could not pass vacuously) and a negative control proving policyFile IS load-bearing on site-map bytes (two buildSiteMap calls differing only in that field produce different JSON).
hardening.notDone: The related repo-wide wart is untouched by design: manifest.source.siteSpecFile / source.reconstructionManifestFile are still recorded at the caller's spelling (visible as absolute paths in data/stripe.com/recon-templates/2026-08-26T17-16-46-409Z/manifest.json and as repo-relative in data/linear.app/recon-templates/2026-08-25T21-53-26-980Z/manifest.json). They are in owned files but out of the brief's scope, and manifest.json sits in the same hashed template dir — so the lineage-spelling class is CLOSED for the policy path and STILL OPEN for the two lineage input paths. Filed as a followUp, not silently fixed.

hardening.finding: 2 — manifest.limitations claimed `structure-only-routes-carry-no-slots:10` while ONE of those 10 stripe routes (/resources/more/virtual-credit-cards-for-businesses-explained, pageId p000012) shares its page with the collection-representative /resources/more/arr-loans-explained, so editing that page's slots DOES change what the 'structure-only' route renders. Prose disclosed it; the machine-readable record did not.
hardening.fix: resolveRoutePolicy now computes `structureOnlySharedPageRoutes` (src/recon-template/route-policy.ts:255-257) and a new pure helper `routePolicyLimitations()` (src/recon-template/route-policy.ts:286-310) emits the companion code `structure-only-routes-sharing-a-slotized-page-do-render-slot-edits:<n>` beside the existing code. compile.ts spreads that helper instead of inlining the codes. The same count is also written to site-map.json / manifest.json routePolicy.structureOnlySharedPageRoutes so it is diffable, not only greppable — optional in the schema and OMITTED when 0, so a policy-free site map keeps the exact bytes it had.
hardening.proof: Measured against the REAL canary inputs, read-only (a throwaway script re-resolving data/stripe.com/recon-templates/2026-08-26T17-16-46-409Z/route-policy.json against the stripe reconstruction, no run directory written): scopeCounts unchanged (core-reconstruct 9 / collection-representative 1 / structure-only 10), structureOnlySharedPageRoutes = 1, and the single shared route is exactly '/resources/more/virtual-credit-cards-for-businesses-explained p000012' — the route the brief named. New codes: ['structure-only-routes-carry-no-slots:10','structure-only-pages-keep-original-content-including-global-slot-values','structure-only-routes-sharing-a-slotized-page-do-render-slot-edits:1'].
hardening.measured: §20 adds a positive case (a fixture route map where /blog/one-alias shares p000002 with the representative /blog/one → count 1 of 3 structure-only routes), a site-map diffability check, and TWO negative controls (drop the alias → code absent and the site-map field omitted; the compiled 2-page fixture does not claim the code while still claiming structure-only-routes-carry-no-slots:1). 5/5 PASS.

Recompiling stripe into a NEW run id would embed the companion code; the brief said not to unless needed, and the count was proved against the same inputs without writing.

hardening.finding: 3 — src/recon-template/route-policy.ts:196-204 incremented ruleHits[i] for EVERY rule that matched a route, including rules that lost the first-match-wins race, so a fully shadowed rule never tripped the unmatched-rule guard.
hardening.severity: MEDIUM (weakened the stage's own stated guarantee)
hardening.fix: The match loop now counts only the DECIDING match and breaks (src/recon-template/route-policy.ts:212-222). The guard's error message says what it now means: 'rule(s) that decide no route … (they match nothing, or every route they match was already decided by an earlier rule)'. The module doc above resolveRoutePolicy was corrected from 'matches no route' to 'DECIDES no route'.
hardening.proof: scripts/smoke-recon-template.ts §20 compiles a policy whose second rule is fully shadowed ([{routePrefix:'/',scope:'core-reconstruct'},{route:'/about',scope:'structure-only'}]) and asserts a TemplateInputError naming /about. Positive control in the same section: an exception ABOVE its sweep is still accepted and still decides (matchedRuleIndex 0 for /blog/one, /blog/two structure-only). §16's pre-existing 'a rule that matches no route is refused' and §17's 'first matching rule wins' both still PASS.
hardening.regressionRisk: Checked against the REAL canary policy before shipping: all 7 rules of data/stripe.com/recon-templates/2026-08-26T17-16-46-409Z/route-policy.json still DECIDE at least one route, and the resolved scope counts are byte-for-byte what the canary recorded (9/1/10).
